correctness.rationale: For each exact profile with exclusive counts \(a,b\) and shared count \(c\), all cleaned assignments are parametrized by the number \(t\) of common goods sent to agent one, with utilities \((a+t,b+c-t)\). Leximin and MNW minimize their absolute difference, giving the exact binomial cardinality formula and \(K_m>1\iff|a-b|<c\); the \(c=0\) and \(c=1\) boundaries are explicit. For iid Bernoulli \(p_m\), the joint-good count has mean \(mp_m^2\) and the exclusive imbalance variance \(2mp_m(1-p_m)\). Chebyshev/Markov and bounded-increment triangular-array CLT yield the zero/one regimes and normal critical window, while binomial entropy bounds and continuous mapping give the distribution of \(\log K_m/m^{1/3}\). An independent exact direct-split checker examined all \(21{,}845\) labeled approval profiles through \(m=7\), with a second unrestricted ternary-assignment comparison on all \(341\) profiles through \(m=4\). The code also checks the generating-function identity. Finite cases support but do not prove the infinite asymptotics.

value.rationale: The optimum-correspondence multiplicity directly quantifies the intrinsic amount of choice before tie-breaking in a natural, axiomatically characterized two-agent resource-allocation model. The competition between \(mp_m^2\) jointly demanded items and \(\sqrt{mp_m}\) exclusive-demand noise creates a sharp, nontrivial cube-root threshold. The exact error-function crossover and full nondegenerate critical log-multiplicity distribution go materially beyond an isolated counting identity or a small finite table and give an interpretable asymptotic phase diagram.
